definition.body: Cepstral-homomorphic-filtering is a signal processing technique that performs filtering by converting a signal to the cepstral domain via log and inverse Fourier transform, applying a filter in the cepstral domain, then reconstructing via forward Fourier transform and exponentiation. Procedure: (1) compute the power spectrum of the input, (2) take logarithm to convert multiplicative convolution to additive, (3) apply inverse Fourier transform to obtain cepstrum, (4) apply homomorphic filter to cepstral coefficients, (5) reconstruct spectrum via forward Fourier transform and exponentiation. Parameters: filter type (lifter, window), lifter cutoff quefrency, filter shape. Persistence: implemented in speech enhancement toolkits, e.g., HTK's cepstral liftering, and described in Oppenheim & Schafer textbooks. e.g.: Oppenheim & Schafer 'Discrete-Time Signal Processing' chapter on homomorphic deconvolution; HTK's cepstral liftering implementation for speech dereverberation; MATLAB's cepstral filtering example for echo removal | not: linear filtering (operates in time/frequency domain, not log-spectrum) [formal: filtratio-cepstralis-homomorphica | substrate: behavior | horizon: a life | explicit: yes]

Procedure: (1) compute the power spectrum of the input, (2) take logarithm to convert multiplicative convolution to additive, (3) apply inverse Fourier transform to obtain cepstrum, (4) apply homomorphic filter to cepstral coefficients, (5) reconstruct spectrum via forward Fourier transform and exponentiation. Parameters: filter type (lifter, window), lifter cutoff quefrency, filter shape. Persistence: implemented in speech enhancement toolkits, e.g., HTK's cepstral liftering, and described in Oppenheim & Schafer textbooks. e.g.: Oppenheim & Schafer 'Discrete-Time Signal Processing' chapter on homomorphic deconvolution; HTK's cepstral liftering implementation for speech dereverberation; MATLAB's cepstral filtering example for echo removal | not: linear filtering (operates in time/frequency domain, not log-spectrum) [formal: filtratio-cepstralis-homomorphica | substrate: behavior | horizon: a life | explicit: yes]

payload.scope: A human-made measure derived from cepstral coefficients: the sum of squares or magnitude of a cepstrum vector, representing the total energy content of the spectral envelope representation.

definition.body: Cepstral-energy is the scalar energy measure computed from cepstral coefficients, defined as the sum of squares of individual coefficients: E = Σ c[i]², optionally weighted by perceptual or quefrency-dependent factors. The procedure: (1) compute cepstral coefficients c[0], c[1], ..., c[M-1] via FFT of the log-power spectrum or DCT of mel-scale filterbank energies; (2) compute the sum of squares of all retained coefficients, optionally applying quefrency weighting w[i] so that E = Σ w[i]·c[i]². Parameters: (1) the number of cepstral coefficients M, (2) optional quefrency weighting scheme, (3) whether DC coefficient c[0] is included. Persistence mechanism: stored as a feature value in speech/speaker recognition systems, computed as part of feature extraction pipelines, documented in audio processing literature. e.g.: the cepstral-energy feature computed alongside MFCCs in Kaldi's featbin/compute-energies; the total cepstral energy used in voice activity detection thresholds; the weighted cepstral energy in speech quality assessment metrics [formal: energy cepstralis | substrate: mind | horizon: a life | explicit: yes]

payload.name: cepstral-entropy
payload.scope: A human-made statistical measure computed from cepstral coefficient distributions: the Shannon entropy of coefficient magnitudes, used to quantify spectral envelope complexity or speech activity in audio signals.

definition.body: Cepstral-entropy is the Shannon entropy measure computed from the magnitude distribution of cepstral coefficients, quantifying the complexity or uncertainty of the spectral envelope representation. The procedure: (1) compute cepstral coefficients c[0], c[1], ..., c[M-1] via FFT of the log-power spectrum or DCT of mel-scale filterbank energies; (2) form a normalized probability distribution p[i] = |c[i]| / Σ|c[j]| over all retained coefficients; (3) compute the Shannon entropy H = -Σ p[i]·log₂(p[i]) over the distribution. Parameters: (1) the number of cepstral coefficients M, (2) the normalization scheme for forming p[i], (3) the log base (typically 2 for bits, or natural log for nats). Persistence mechanism: stored as a feature value in speech/speaker recognition systems, computed as part of feature extraction pipelines for VAD and classification. e.g.: the cepstral-entropy feature used in voice activity detection thresholds in Kaldi; the Shannon entropy of MFCC distributions in speech vs. non-speech classification; the cepstral-entropy metric in speaker diarization for utterance boundary detection [formal: entropia cepstralis | substrate: mind | horizon: a life | explicit: yes]

payload.name: prediction-gain
payload.scope: People made prediction gain to quantify how much of a speech signal's energy is captured by linear prediction, enabling excitation characterization and frame quality assessment in speech coders.

definition.body: Prediction gain measures how much of a signal's variance is predictable from its past samples using linear prediction, computed as the ratio of the signal's autocorrelation-based energy to the prediction error energy. The procedure: (1) compute the linear prediction coefficients a_k for the speech frame via the Yule-Walker equations or the Burg algorithm; (2) compute the prediction error energy E_p = R[0] - Σ(a_k · R[k]) for k=1..p, where R[k] is the autocorrelation at lag k; (3) the prediction gain is G = R[0] / E_p, the ratio of total frame energy to error energy. Parameters: (1) the analysis frame, (2) the prediction order p, (3) the autocorrelation method. Persistence: stored and transmitted as a frame-level feature in speech coders (G.729, AMR), used in VoIP for frame quality assessment, and taught in speech processing as a fundamental LPC analysis result. e.g.: the prediction gain computed in ITU-T G.729 for excitation characterization; the LP prediction gain measured in AMR codec mode selection; the ratio of frame energy to residual energy in Kaldi's lpc computation pipeline | not: the prediction error variance (which is the denominator only); the all-pole filter gain (which is the spectral envelope normalization, not the predictability ratio) [formal: praedictionis gain | substrate: mind | horizon: a life | explicit: yes]

payload.name: speech-synthesis
payload.scope: People made speech synthesis to generate natural-sounding artificial speech from textual or linguistic representations, enabling applications from text-to-speech systems to vocoder-based waveform reconstruction.

definition.body: Speech synthesis is a human-made signal processing procedure that generates artificial speech waveforms from linguistic representations (text, phonemes, or prosodic features). The procedure varies by approach: (1) concatenative synthesis selects and concatenates recorded speech units at word/phone boundaries; (2) parametric synthesis uses acoustic models (HMM-based HTS, Gaussian mixture models) to generate cepstral trajectories then applies a vocoder (STRAIGHT, WORLD, overlap-add); (3) neural synthesis uses deep learning (Tacotron, WaveNet, FastSpeech) to generate waveforms or spectral features directly. Parameters: (1) the input representation (text, IPA, phonemes), (2) the synthesis method, (3) the vocoder type, (4) the target voice characteristics. Persistence: implemented in TTS toolkits (Kaldi, MaryTTS, Festival, Coqui TTS), deployed in commercial systems (Amazon Polly, Google TTS), standardized through benchmarks (VCTK, LJSpeech), and sustained by open-source repositories and academic research. e.g.: the HMM-based speech synthesis (HTS) system from CMU for state-selection; the Tacotron 2 neural TTS system for mel-spectrogram generation; the FastSpeech 2 parallel TTS model for duration-controlled synthesis | not: speech-recognition (converts speech to text, opposite direction); voice-activity-detection (determines presence of speech, does not synthesize) [formal: synthetica vocis | substrate: mind | horizon: generations | explicit: yes]
